subject: body
title: Everyday and Sometimes Foods
about: Everyday foods and sometimes foods: no food is bad, but candy, chips, cookies, cake and fries are for once in a while, what makes a food a sometimes food (lots of added sugar or salt), candy's quick energy that fades, a treat at a party is fine and a treat at a friend's house gets a thank you, a crunchy everyday snack, the label that shows added sugar, why salty snacks make you thirsty, one treat not changing the rest of the day, and where sugar comes from. NC 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them) and 1.NPA.1.3 (where foods come from). Read it together with no food called bad and no talk about size or weight, just everyday and sometimes.
tip: When he asks for a treat, answer with the words: is that an everyday food or a sometimes food?

cards.q: Foods you can eat every day, like fruit, rice and bread, are called...?
cards.note: Everyday foods give your body what it needs. Most of what you eat should be everyday foods.

cards.q: Candy, chips, cookies and cake are small treats for once in a while. What do we call them?
cards.note: Sometimes foods taste great but give your body little of what it needs to grow. They are for once in a while, not every day.

cards.q: Cake is a sometimes food. Can you ever have cake?
cards.note: No food is off limits; sometimes foods are just not for every day. Enjoy a slice at a party!

cards.q: It is a birthday party and there is cake. What do you do?
cards.note: A treat at a party is part of the fun. Enjoy it, then back to everyday foods tomorrow.

cards.q: Candy gives you a quick bit of energy. Does that energy last a long time?
cards.note: Candy's energy comes and goes quickly. Whole grains, fruit and protein foods give energy that lasts all morning.

cards.q: Candy, soda and chips are sometimes foods because they have lots of added...?
cards.note: Lots of added sugar or salt is what makes a food a sometimes food. Everyday foods bring vitamins, fiber and protein instead.

cards.q: At a friend's house, their grown-up gives you a cookie at snack time. What do you say?
cards.note: Every family has its own treats. A grown-up offers, you say thank you and enjoy it; nobody needs a lecture about food.

cards.q: Which snack is crunchy and an everyday food?
cards.note: Carrots crunch like chips and carry vitamins. Dip them in hummus or yogurt.

cards.q: Many boxed foods have sugar added. Where can a grown-up read what is inside?
cards.note: The ingredient list shows what is inside. Sugar hides under names like syrup too.

cards.q: Chips and pretzels are salty. What do salty snacks make you feel?
cards.note: Salt makes you thirsty. Have a glass of water with salty snacks.

cards.q: You had cake at a party today. What do you eat at dinner tonight?
cards.note: One treat does not change the rest of the day. Dinner is dinner: everyday foods, like always.

cards.q: How often do we eat a sometimes food?
cards.note: Not every day. A sometimes food is a treat, not a habit.

cards.q: Sugar is made from the sweet juice of a tall grass plant. What is the plant called?
cards.note: Sugar comes from sugar cane, a tall grass, and from sugar beets, a root. Honey is made by bees, and fruit has its own sugar.

cards.q: Fries are a sometimes food. What could you have most days instead?
cards.note: A baked potato or corn on the cob is a vegetable. Fries now and then are fine too.

cards.q: Which one is a sometimes food?
cards.note: Doughnuts are sweet and fried. A yummy treat for once in a while.

cards.q: Which one is an everyday food?
cards.note: Toast is grains. Top it with mashed banana, or peanut butter if nuts are safe for you, for a tasty start.
